meta.title: Quanta Services — Duke Austin's electric-and-renewable specialty contractor through the AI data centre and grid-investment cycle
meta.abstract: Quanta Services is the largest specialty contractor in the North American electric power, renewable energy, and pipeline infrastructure markets, listed on the NYSE under the ticker PWR. Founded in 1997 as a roll-up of regional electrical contractors and headquartered in Houston, Texas, the company built its scale through a multi-decade acquisition programme covering transmission and distribution (T&D) line construction, substation construction, underground utility construction, solar and wind project construction, and broader specialty infrastructure construction. Under CEO Duke Austin (since 2016, with the company since the 2003 PAR Electrical acquisition), Quanta has positioned through three interlocking cycles: the multi-year utility grid investment cycle driven by aging infrastructure replacement and weather-resilience hardening; the renewable energy capacity build-out driven by the Inflation Reduction Act and broader state-level renewable energy mandates; and the more recent AI data centre electrical infrastructure cycle driven by the substantial new electrical interconnection and substation requirements of hyperscaler AI deployments. The 2021 Blattner Energy acquisition for approximately $2.7 billion substantially scaled the utility-scale renewable energy construction position; the 2022 Cupertino Electric acquisition added the electrical contracting capability across the data centre and broader commercial customer base. Revenue trajectory through fiscal 2020-2024 has reflected the multi-segment growth: 2020 revenue was approximately $11.2 billion, 2022 was approximately $17.1 billion, and 2024 was approximately $23.7 billion. The Electric Infrastructure segment is the largest single segment; the Renewable Energy Infrastructure segment has been the most rapidly scaling; the Underground Utility and Infrastructure segment provides the broader infrastructure diversification.

Founded in 1997 as a roll-up of regional electrical contractors and headquartered in Houston, Texas, the company built its scale through a multi-decade acquisition programme covering transmission and distribution (T&D) line construction, substation construction, underground utility construction, solar and wind project construction, and broader specialty infrastructure construction. The 2021 Blattner Energy acquisition for approximately $2.7 billion substantially scaled the utility-scale renewable energy construction position; the 2022 Cupertino Electric acquisition added the electrical contracting capability across the data centre and broader commercial customer base.

chapters.title: Snapshot
chapters.body:
Quanta Services reached the frozen window with a scale that the 2024-only framing in the prior draft no longer captured. Full-year 2025 revenue was $28.48 billion, up from $23.67 billion in 2024, while year-end remaining performance obligations were $23.76 billion and total backlog was $43.98 billion. First-quarter 2026 revenue then rose to $7.87 billion and total backlog to $48.5 billion, prompting management to raise 2026 revenue guidance to $34.7 billion to $35.2 billion. [Q4 & FY2025 Results](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/390/quanta-services-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results) [Q1 2026 Results](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/396/quanta-services-reports-first-quarter-2026-results)

That backdrop also changed the public-market framing. On Quanta's investor quote page, the last trade before the frozen date was $723.44 on May 22, 2026; the same company-hosted quote widget showed 150,060,149 shares outstanding and a market capitalization of $108.56 billion. [Quote and Chart](https://investors.quantaservices.com/stock-data/quote-chart)

## The Current Segment Architecture

The prior draft correctly noted that Quanta reported three segments through fiscal 2024, but the snapshot date sat well after the reporting re-cut. For 2024, Electric Power Infrastructure Solutions generated $11.17 billion of revenue, Renewable Energy Infrastructure Solutions $7.85 billion, and Underground Utility and Infrastructure Solutions $4.66 billion. Beginning with the quarter ended March 31, 2025, however, Quanta combined the former electric-power and renewable businesses into a single Electric Infrastructure Solutions segment, leaving Underground Utility and Infrastructure Solutions as the second reportable segment. On that recast basis, 2025 revenue was $23.00 billion in Electric and $5.48 billion in Underground and Infrastructure. [Q4 & FY2024 Results](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/371/quanta-services-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2024-results) [Q1 2025 Results](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/374/quanta-services-reports-first-quarter-2025-results) [Q4 & FY2025 Results](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/390/quanta-services-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results)

That mattered because the dossier's underlying thesis was not only that Quanta was large, but that it had become structurally harder to classify as a plain-vanilla transmission contractor. By the frozen date, Quanta's own disclosures described the company as serving utility, power generation, load center, communications, pipeline and energy markets. The segment recast was therefore more than an accounting cleanup: it reflected a business that now bundled traditional grid work, renewable generation and interconnection, data-center electrical scope and, after later acquisitions, parts of the mechanical critical path serving large-load customers. [Q1 2026 Results](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/396/quanta-services-reports-first-quarter-2026-results) [Dynamic Systems Acquisition](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/380/quanta-services-acquires-dynamic-systems-a-premier-turnkey-mechanical-and-process-infrastructure-solutions-provider)

## Leadership and the Current Operating Shape

The prior draft's leadership section was materially stale. Earl C. "Duke" Austin had served as president and chief executive officer since March 14, 2016, after serving as chief operating officer from January 2013. Quanta's current management materials said he had joined the Quanta executive team in 2009, after running North Houston Pole Line, a Quanta operating unit, and that he held a B.S. in Business Management/Accounting from Sam Houston State University. Jayshree Desai did not arrive from ChampionX in late 2022; Quanta said she joined as chief corporate development officer in January 2020 and was elevated to chief financial officer effective July 2022. [CEO Transition](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/202/quanta-services-announces-ceo-transition-chief-operating-officer-earl-duke-austin-named-chief-executive-officer) [Management Team](https://investors.quantaservices.com/company-information/management-team) [Executive Transitions](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/319/quanta-services-announces-planned-executive-transitions)

Governance had changed as well. By the 2026 proxy, Quanta had a separate independent chairman rather than the lead-independent-director structure described in the prior draft, with Doyle N. Beneby serving as chairman of the board. The board slate for the May 21, 2026 annual meeting included Beneby, Warner Baxter, Bernard Fried, Worthing Jackman, Joseph Kim, Holli Ladhani, Jo-ann dePass Olsovsky, R. Scott Rowe, Martha Wyrsch and Austin; Quanta then separately announced on May 22, 2026 that Joseph Kim had joined the board. [2026 Proxy Statement](https://investors.quantaservices.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001193125-26-150293/d118470ddef14a.htm) [Joseph Kim Joins Board](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/398/joseph-kim-joins-quanta-services-board-of-directors)

## The Acquisition Arc: Blattner, Cupertino and Dynamic Systems

The modern Quanta was still best understood through acquisitions, but the timing in the prior draft needed correction. Quanta announced the Blattner transaction in June 2021 at an enterprise value of about $2.7 billion and completed it in October 2021, adding what it described as the leading utility-scale renewable contractor in North America. The Inflation Reduction Act was enacted later, on August 16, 2022, so the policy tailwind reinforced the deal after signing rather than explaining it beforehand. [Blattner Announcement](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/301/quanta-services-to-acquire-blattner-holding-company-) [H.R. 5376](https://www.congress.gov/bill/117th-congress/house-bill/5376)

Cupertino Electric closed on July 18, 2024, not in 2022. Quanta disclosed consideration of roughly $1.54 billion, comprising about $1.3 billion of cash, approximately 883,000 Quanta shares and a potential earnout of up to $200 million. The release also said Cupertino had installed electrical systems in more than 20 million square feet of data centers and had a 25-year working history with global technology-industry leaders. [Cupertino Electric Acquisition](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/360/quanta-services-acquires-cupertino-electric-inc-a-premier-electrical-infrastructure-solutions-provider-to-the-technology-and-renewable-energy-industries)

Quanta then widened the load-center thesis again in July 2025 when it completed the acquisition of Dynamic Systems for roughly $1.35 billion of upfront consideration, consisting of about $1.15 billion of cash and about $200 million of Quanta stock, plus a potential earnout of up to $216 million. Dynamic Systems gave Quanta a mechanical and process-infrastructure platform with exposure to technology, semiconductor, healthcare and other load-center markets. [Dynamic Systems Acquisition](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/380/quanta-services-acquires-dynamic-systems-a-premier-turnkey-mechanical-and-process-infrastructure-solutions-provider)

## Backlog: Big, But Not All the Same Kind of Revenue Certainty

The prior draft also treated backlog as a single block of contracted visibility. Quanta's March 31, 2026 10-Q showed a more nuanced composition. Of the $48.47 billion backlog figure corresponding to the headline "$48.5 billion" release number, $26.24 billion was remaining performance obligations and $22.23 billion was estimated orders under master service agreements and short-term, non-fixed price contracts. Put differently, just over half of the reported backlog sat in formal RPO, while the balance rested in Quanta's estimate of work expected under recurring frameworks and shorter-duration arrangements. [Q1 2026 10-Q](https://investors.quantaservices.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001050915-26-000016/pwr-20260331.htm)

## Open Questions for This Dossier

That was the proper starting point for the chapters that follow. The question was no longer whether Quanta had reached scale; it plainly had. The harder question was whether the enlarged Electric segment, Cupertino's technology relationships, Dynamic Systems' mechanical critical-path capabilities and the company's rising mix of large-load and power-generation work could convert record backlog into durable, high-quality earnings without stretching execution, labor or supply-chain discipline. A second question, made clearer by the 10-Q backlog table, was how much of the headline figure should be read as hard contractual RPO and how much as repeat business under MSAs that still carried timing and forecasting judgment. Those were more precise issues than the prior draft had framed, and they mattered more by May 2026 than the older 2024 snapshot alone. [Q1 2026 Results](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/396/quanta-services-reports-first-quarter-2026-results) [Q1 2026 10-Q](https://investors.quantaservices.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001050915-26-000016/pwr-20260331.htm)

chapters.title: From 1997 roll-up through Austin succession, Blattner, Cupertino, and AI inflection
chapters.body:
## The 1997 Formation and 1998 IPO

Quanta's origin story was earlier and more specific than the prior draft suggested. In its October 1998 prospectus, the company said it had been founded in August 1997 and that in February 1998 it was formed through the combination of four founding businesses: PAR Electrical Contractors, Union Power Construction, TRANS TECH Electric and Potelco. The same filing said Quanta completed its initial public offering in February 1998 and then used the public-company platform to continue a disciplined acquisition program in what it described as a highly fragmented specialty electrical and telecommunications contracting market. [1998 Prospectus](https://investors.quantaservices.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0000899243-98-001959/424B2.txt)

That detail mattered because it corrected two errors embedded in the prior chronology. First, PAR was not a 2003 bolt-on; it was one of the four founding businesses around the IPO. Second, the early Quanta model was decentralized from the outset. The prospectus said acquired operators would remain responsible for profitability and growth at their own businesses while the parent centralized strategy, acquisitions, financing, insurance, investor relations and benefit plans. That operating model remained visible in Quanta's public disclosures nearly three decades later. [1998 Prospectus](https://investors.quantaservices.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0000899243-98-001959/424B2.txt)

## Duke Austin's Actual Entry Path

The prior draft also overstated the role of a nonexistent 2003 PAR transaction in Duke Austin's biography. Quanta's March 2016 CEO-transition release said Austin had joined Quanta in 2001, had served as president of North Houston Pole Line from 2001 until September 2009, led the oil and gas division from October 2009 to May 2011, oversaw power and pipeline operations from January 2011, became chief operating officer in January 2013 and was named president and chief executive officer on March 14, 2016. Quanta's management page further said he joined the Quanta executive team in 2009 and was a graduate of Sam Houston State University. [CEO Transition](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/202/quanta-services-announces-ceo-transition-chief-operating-officer-earl-duke-austin-named-chief-executive-officer) [Management Team](https://investors.quantaservices.com/company-information/management-team)

That distinction mattered analytically. Austin did not arrive as the leader of an acquired outside franchise that later swallowed the rest of Quanta culturally. He rose through an operating unit already inside the Quanta orbit, then through the corporate operating hierarchy. The strategic posture visible by the frozen window -- long-duration customer relationships, labor scarcity awareness, opportunistic but operationally anchored acquisitions -- looked more like an extension of the original decentralized model than a break from it. [1998 Prospectus](https://investors.quantaservices.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0000899243-98-001959/424B2.txt) [CEO Transition](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/202/quanta-services-announces-ceo-transition-chief-operating-officer-earl-duke-austin-named-chief-executive-officer)

## Blattner and the Renewable Turn

The first transformative deal of the current era was Blattner. Quanta announced the acquisition in June 2021 at an enterprise value of approximately $2.7 billion and described Blattner as the leading utility-scale renewable energy infrastructure solutions provider in North America. The deal closed in October 2021 and created the real financial scale behind what was then Quanta's Renewable Energy Infrastructure Solutions segment. [Blattner Announcement](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/301/quanta-services-to-acquire-blattner-holding-company-) [Q4 & FY2024 Results](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/371/quanta-services-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2024-results)

Only after that came the federal policy accelerant. The Inflation Reduction Act became law on August 16, 2022. That sequencing mattered because Quanta had already committed capital to renewable-scale construction capability before the tax-credit regime was expanded and extended. The law strengthened the demand backdrop for Blattner, but the deal itself predated the statute. [H.R. 5376](https://www.congress.gov/bill/117th-congress/house-bill/5376) [Blattner Announcement](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/301/quanta-services-to-acquire-blattner-holding-company-)

## Cupertino, Then Dynamic Systems

The second major turn was Cupertino Electric. Quanta completed that acquisition on July 18, 2024 for about $1.54 billion, comprised of roughly $1.3 billion of cash, approximately 883,000 Quanta shares and a potential earnout of up to $200 million. Cupertino was not a generic commercial electrical contractor in Quanta's own telling. The release emphasized its inside-electric and power-systems capabilities, its more than 20 million square feet of completed data-center electrical installations and its 25-year history with global technology-industry leaders. [Cupertino Electric Acquisition](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/360/quanta-services-acquires-cupertino-electric-inc-a-premier-electrical-infrastructure-solutions-provider-to-the-technology-and-renewable-energy-industries)

The next addition came a year later. Quanta completed the acquisition of Dynamic Systems on July 25, 2025 and announced it publicly on July 31, 2025. It paid about $1.35 billion of upfront consideration and described the target as a large turnkey mechanical and process-infrastructure provider to technology, semiconductor, healthcare and other load-center markets. In effect, Quanta used Dynamic Systems to extend the Cupertino logic from electrical scope into part of the mechanical critical path of large-load facilities. [Dynamic Systems Acquisition](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/380/quanta-services-acquires-dynamic-systems-a-premier-turnkey-mechanical-and-process-infrastructure-solutions-provider)

## The Historical Arc by the Frozen Date

By the frozen date, Quanta's history no longer looked like a simple roll-up that had grown large by repetition. The first phase was the 1997-1998 formation and IPO, built around combining founding contractors under a decentralized operating model. The second phase was Austin's climb through Quanta's operating structure and his 2016 elevation to CEO. The third phase was the company's decision to buy scarce operating capability rather than wait to build it organically: first renewable scale through Blattner in 2021, then data-center electrical capability through Cupertino in 2024, then mechanical load-center scope through Dynamic Systems in 2025. Those three phases explained more of the business visible in May 2026 than the older PAR-centered narrative did. [1998 Prospectus](https://investors.quantaservices.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0000899243-98-001959/424B2.txt) [CEO Transition](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/202/quanta-services-announces-ceo-transition-chief-operating-officer-earl-duke-austin-named-chief-executive-officer) [Blattner Announcement](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/301/quanta-services-to-acquire-blattner-holding-company-) [Cupertino Electric Acquisition](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/360/quanta-services-acquires-cupertino-electric-inc-a-premier-electrical-infrastructure-solutions-provider-to-the-technology-and-renewable-energy-industries) [Dynamic Systems Acquisition](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/380/quanta-services-acquires-dynamic-systems-a-premier-turnkey-mechanical-and-process-infrastructure-solutions-provider)

chapters.title: Electric Power Infrastructure, Renewable Energy Infrastructure, Underground Utility
chapters.body:
## The 2024 Three-Segment Base

The prior draft got the broad shape right but materially misstated the segment figures. For fiscal 2024, Quanta reported $11.17 billion of revenue in Electric Power Infrastructure Solutions, $7.85 billion in Renewable Energy Infrastructure Solutions and $4.66 billion in Underground Utility and Infrastructure Solutions, for consolidated revenue of $23.67 billion. Those figures mattered because they showed the renewable business was already much larger than the draft's implied $6.4 billion and the underground business materially larger than the roughly $3.1 billion cited there. [Q4 & FY2024 Results](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/371/quanta-services-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2024-results)

| 2024 segment | Revenue | Share of 2024 revenue |
|---|---:|---:|
| Electric Power Infrastructure Solutions | $11.17B | 47.2% |
| Renewable Energy Infrastructure Solutions | $7.85B | 33.1% |
| Underground Utility and Infrastructure Solutions | $4.66B | 19.7% |

Those categories also mapped to meaningfully different scopes of work. In the 2025 10-K, Quanta said the electric business covered overhead and underground transmission and distribution, substations, grid hardening, smart-grid installations, emergency restoration and electrical systems for large load centers such as data centers and advanced manufacturing facilities. The renewable business covered engineering, procurement, construction, repowering and maintenance for utility-scale wind, solar, hydropower and battery storage. Underground and Infrastructure covered gas utility systems, pipeline integrity and replacement, civil solutions and selected industrial services. [2025 10-K](https://investors.quantaservices.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001050915-26-000006/pwr-20251231.htm)

## The 2025 Recast to Two Segments

Beginning with the quarter ended March 31, 2025, Quanta folded the former electric-power and renewable businesses into a single Electric Infrastructure Solutions segment and retained Underground Utility and Infrastructure Solutions as the second reportable segment. On the recast basis included in the 2025 results, 2024 Electric revenue was $19.01 billion and Underground and Infrastructure $4.66 billion; by 2025 those figures had increased to $23.00 billion and $5.48 billion, respectively. [Q1 2025 Results](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/374/quanta-services-reports-first-quarter-2025-results) [Q4 & FY2025 Results](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/390/quanta-services-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results)

| Recast segment view | 2024 revenue | 2025 revenue |
|---|---:|---:|
| Electric Infrastructure Solutions | $19.01B | $23.00B |
| Underground Utility and Infrastructure Solutions | $4.66B | $5.48B |

That recast did not merely tidy the reporting lines. It formally acknowledged that Quanta no longer viewed utility transmission, renewable-generation construction and parts of large-load electrical infrastructure as separate strategic silos. The 2025 10-K said the Electric segment also included most of the financial results from Quanta's advanced training facility and postsecondary educational institution, certain transformer, circuit-breaker and other manufacturing operations, and its share of selected infrastructure affiliates including LUMA in Puerto Rico. In Quanta's own 2024 sustainability reporting, Cupertino's inside-electric capabilities were likewise presented alongside the group's grid and renewable offerings as part of one electrical infrastructure system. [2025 10-K](https://investors.quantaservices.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001050915-26-000006/pwr-20251231.htm) [Quanta Sustainability 2024](https://sustainability.quantaservices.com/)

## Electric Infrastructure: Utility Grid, Renewable Generation and Load-Center Electrical Scope

Under the current reporting structure, Electric was the heart of the enterprise. In the first quarter of 2026, Electric generated $6.47 billion of revenue, or 82.1% of the total, versus $1.41 billion for Underground and Infrastructure. The segment now housed the old transmission-and-distribution core, the Blattner renewable platform and the inside-electric and power-systems capabilities acquired with Cupertino. [Q1 2026 Results](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/396/quanta-services-reports-first-quarter-2026-results)

That broadened electric scope was visible in Quanta's own language during 2024 and 2025. In the third-quarter 2024 release, management said Cupertino integration was progressing well and described positive customer response to a combined electrical offering for technology and data-center work. By the 2025 10-K, Quanta said it believed it was positioned to provide turnkey infrastructure solutions for large-load facilities, including critical-path low-voltage electrical scope inside data centers, high-voltage substations, transformers and transmission interconnections to connect those facilities to the grid, and generation infrastructure needed to power them. [Q3 2024 Results](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/367/quanta-services-reports-third-quarter-2024-results) [2025 10-K](https://investors.quantaservices.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001050915-26-000006/pwr-20251231.htm)

## Renewable Energy Was Not a Sidecar Business

The earlier draft understated how big the renewable business had already become before the reporting re-cut. Renewable Energy Infrastructure Solutions produced $7.85 billion of 2024 revenue and $667.1 million of 2024 operating income, up from $6.17 billion and $477.2 million, respectively, in 2023. Even after Quanta stopped reporting renewables as a stand-alone segment, the 2024 sustainability materials still highlighted $7.846 billion of renewable-energy infrastructure solutions revenue and a 2024 construction tally of 10,330 megawatts of utility-scale wind and solar plus 1,577 megawatts of utility-scale battery storage, or nearly 11.9 gigawatts combined. [Q4 & FY2024 Results](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/371/quanta-services-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2024-results) [2024 Sustainability Report Metrics](https://sustainability.quantaservices.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/2024-Quanta-Sustainability-Report-Pages.pdf)

That was important for the dossier because it changed the analytical burden. The question was not whether Quanta had renewable exposure; it plainly did, at scale. The question was whether the company could keep monetizing that scale after integrating renewables into the broader Electric segment and while allocating more management attention to data centers, generation, interconnection and load-growth programs. [Q4 & FY2025 Results](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/390/quanta-services-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results)

## Underground and Infrastructure: Still Smaller, No Longer Merely Ballast

The underground business remained the smaller reporting unit, but it was not as marginal as the prior draft implied. It contributed $4.66 billion of revenue in 2024, $5.48 billion in 2025 and $1.41 billion in the first quarter of 2026. Quanta's filings positioned the segment around gas distribution and transmission, water and wastewater, communications, pipeline integrity and civil solutions, but by 2025 the description had widened further: the 10-K said Underground and Infrastructure also served midstream and downstream industrial energy markets and provided turnkey mechanical, plumbing and process infrastructure solutions for large-load facilities in the technology, semiconductor, healthcare and other industries. [Q4 & FY2024 Results](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/371/quanta-services-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2024-results) [Q4 & FY2025 Results](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/390/quanta-services-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results) [2025 10-K](https://investors.quantaservices.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001050915-26-000006/pwr-20251231.htm)

The Dynamic Systems acquisition made that widening measurable. Quanta said Dynamic would sit in Underground and Infrastructure, brought roughly 2,400 employees, and was expected to contribute $1.25 billion to $1.45 billion of 2026 revenue and $125 million to $175 million of 2026 adjusted EBITDA. That assignment was analytically significant. It meant the second segment was no longer only gas, water and conduit work; it had become the reporting home for a mechanical platform serving technology, semiconductor, healthcare and other load-center facilities. In other words, the two-segment structure was not a reduction in complexity. It was Quanta's way of grouping a growing collection of adjacent infrastructure scopes under broader execution umbrellas. [Dynamic Systems Acquisition](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/380/quanta-services-acquires-dynamic-systems-a-premier-turnkey-mechanical-and-process-infrastructure-solutions-provider)

chapters.title: Revenue trajectory, segment economics, M&A capital structure
chapters.body:
## The Revenue Arc

The prior draft correctly identified a structural acceleration in Quanta's revenue base, but it misdated one of the key drivers. Cupertino did not contribute in 2022; the acquisition closed on July 18, 2024. The actual annual revenue progression was $12.97 billion in 2021, $17.07 billion in 2022, $20.88 billion in 2023, $23.67 billion in 2024 and $28.48 billion in 2025. That sequence still captured a dramatic step-up, but it was driven first by Blattner's full-period contribution and organic growth across grid and renewables, then by the 2024 and 2025 load-center additions rather than any 2022 Cupertino consolidation. [Q4 & FY2024 Results](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/371/quanta-services-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2024-results) [Q4 & FY2025 Results](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/390/quanta-services-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results) [Cupertino Electric Acquisition](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/360/quanta-services-acquires-cupertino-electric-inc-a-premier-electrical-infrastructure-solutions-provider-to-the-technology-and-renewable-energy-industries)

| Fiscal year | Revenue |
|---|---:|
| 2019 | $12.11B |
| 2020 | $11.20B |
| 2021 | $12.97B |
| 2022 | $17.07B |
| 2023 | $20.88B |
| 2024 | $23.67B |
| 2025 | $28.48B |

## Segment Economics on the Recast Basis

The recast segment tables in the 2025 release showed where that growth sat economically. Electric Infrastructure Solutions produced $23.00 billion of 2025 revenue and $2.36 billion of operating income, holding an operating margin of 10.3%. Underground and Infrastructure produced $5.48 billion of revenue and $398.3 million of operating income, for a 7.3% operating margin. In 2024, on the recast basis, Electric had already been $19.01 billion of revenue and $1.96 billion of operating income, while Underground and Infrastructure was $4.66 billion of revenue and $265.0 million of operating income. [Q4 & FY2025 Results](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/390/quanta-services-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results)

Those figures clarified two things that the prior draft left hazy. First, Quanta's earnings engine was still overwhelmingly Electric, even after the company broadened its end markets. Second, the underground platform was improving economically rather than merely providing volume ballast. That mattered because the newer mechanical and process-infrastructure capability acquired with Dynamic Systems was placed inside the latter segment, where margin and mix were already moving the right way into 2026. [Dynamic Systems Acquisition](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/380/quanta-services-acquires-dynamic-systems-a-premier-turnkey-mechanical-and-process-infrastructure-solutions-provider) [Q1 2026 Results](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/396/quanta-services-reports-first-quarter-2026-results)

## Cash Generation and Conversion

The cash profile also remained strong. In 2024, Quanta reported $2.08 billion of cash flow from operations and $1.55 billion of free cash flow. In 2025, those figures improved to $2.23 billion and $1.67 billion, respectively. The first quarter of 2026 remained solid, though seasonally smaller, at $391.7 million of operating cash flow and $184.4 million of free cash flow. [Q4 & FY2024 Results](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/371/quanta-services-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2024-results) [Q4 & FY2025 Results](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/390/quanta-services-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results) [Q1 2026 Results](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/396/quanta-services-reports-first-quarter-2026-results)

That cash generation mattered because Quanta's acquisition pace had not slowed. The company told investors in the first-quarter 2026 release that it had completed eight acquisitions during 2025, and the proxy likewise described 2025 as a year in which Quanta expanded mechanical infrastructure, civil solutions, aviation services and a utility-pole supply-chain investment. The balance-sheet story therefore was not that Quanta had paused to digest prior deals. It was that the business was producing enough cash to keep expanding the platform while defending its guidance and backlog profile. [Q1 2026 Results](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/396/quanta-services-reports-first-quarter-2026-results) [2026 Proxy Statement](https://investors.quantaservices.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001193125-26-150293/d118470ddef14a.htm)

## M&A Capital Structure: What Was Actually Disclosed

The financial terms that could be verified from primary sources were more concrete than some of the draft's higher-level characterizations. Cupertino's upfront purchase price was about $1.54 billion, comprising about $1.3 billion of cash and about 883,000 Quanta shares, with a potential earnout of up to $200 million. Dynamic Systems carried about $1.35 billion of upfront consideration, including about $1.15 billion of cash and about $200 million of Quanta stock, plus a potential earnout of up to $216 million. Quanta said it funded the cash portion of Dynamic Systems with drawings under its commercial paper program and existing senior credit facility. [Cupertino Electric Acquisition](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/360/quanta-services-acquires-cupertino-electric-inc-a-premier-electrical-infrastructure-solutions-provider-to-the-technology-and-renewable-energy-industries) [Dynamic Systems Acquisition](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/380/quanta-services-acquires-dynamic-systems-a-premier-turnkey-mechanical-and-process-infrastructure-solutions-provider)

The company gave less financing detail in the public acquisition announcement for Blattner than the prior draft implied, but it did clearly disclose the approximately $2.7 billion enterprise value and the strategic rationale: add scale in utility-scale renewables. That made Blattner, Cupertino and Dynamic Systems three different capital-allocation bets on three different constrained scopes of infrastructure labor: renewable generation and interconnection, inside electric and power systems for large-load facilities, and mechanical/process critical-path systems. [Blattner Announcement](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/301/quanta-services-to-acquire-blattner-holding-company-) [Cupertino Electric Acquisition](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/360/quanta-services-acquires-cupertino-electric-inc-a-premier-electrical-infrastructure-solutions-provider-to-the-technology-and-renewable-energy-industries) [Dynamic Systems Acquisition](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/380/quanta-services-acquires-dynamic-systems-a-premier-turnkey-mechanical-and-process-infrastructure-solutions-provider)

## The Forward Financial Frame

By April 2026, Quanta's financial frame had moved beyond the older "$26 billion in 2025" language that appeared in the prior draft. The company had actually delivered $28.48 billion for 2025, started 2026 with $7.87 billion of first-quarter revenue and raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $34.7 billion to $35.2 billion. The issue for investors by the frozen date was not whether Quanta could still grow the top line. The issue was how much of that growth could hold attractive incremental returns as load-center work, generation projects and broader supply-chain investments became a larger share of the mix. [Q4 & FY2025 Results](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/390/quanta-services-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results) [Q1 2026 Results](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/396/quanta-services-reports-first-quarter-2026-results)

chapters.title: Post-Austin quarters through Blattner, Cupertino, AI inflection
chapters.body:
## The Sequence Was Operational Before It Was Narrative

The prior draft treated Quanta's earnings story as though it were a smooth march from renewables to AI infrastructure. The actual sequence disclosed by the company was more granular. Blattner was the first step: Quanta announced the deal in June 2021 and completed it in October 2021, giving the company a scaled renewable-construction platform before the Inflation Reduction Act became law in August 2022. The company then reshaped senior management in 2022, announcing in May that Derrick Jensen would move to executive vice president - business operations and that Jayshree Desai, who had joined in January 2020 as chief corporate development officer, would become chief financial officer effective in July 2022. [Blattner Announcement](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/301/quanta-services-to-acquire-blattner-holding-company-) [Executive Transitions](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/319/quanta-services-announces-planned-executive-transitions) [H.R. 5376](https://www.congress.gov/bill/117th-congress/house-bill/5376)

That chronology mattered because it showed Quanta's eventual data-center exposure was not simply grafted onto a pre-existing renewable story by coincidence. The company first bought renewable scale, then stabilized its leadership bench, then bought Cupertino Electric in July 2024, and only after that began publicly describing the convergence of utility, renewable and technology end markets in increasingly direct language. [Cupertino Electric Acquisition](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/360/quanta-services-acquires-cupertino-electric-inc-a-premier-electrical-infrastructure-solutions-provider-to-the-technology-and-renewable-energy-industries) [Q3 2024 Results](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/367/quanta-services-reports-third-quarter-2024-results)

## Cupertino's Integration Was Visible in the Releases

The first-quarter and second-quarter 2024 releases did not yet contain Cupertino, because the deal had not closed. By the third-quarter 2024 release, however, Quanta said Cupertino integration was progressing well and reported positive customer response to what it called a comprehensive, critical-path electrical infrastructure solution for the technology and data-center industry. That was the first fully supportable primary-source marker that the company itself saw the large-load thesis as more than an investor talking point. [Q3 2024 Results](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/367/quanta-services-reports-third-quarter-2024-results)

The fourth-quarter 2024 release then broadened the framing. Austin said accelerating demand for power and infrastructure solutions was reshaping the industry and that Quanta was at the center of that transformation; he also tied 2025 guidance to continued record backlog. The company simultaneously disclosed $34.54 billion of year-end backlog, $16.76 billion of year-end RPO and the decision to reorganize into two reportable segments beginning in the March 2025 quarter. [Q4 & FY2024 Results](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/371/quanta-services-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2024-results)

## 2025 Was the Consolidation Year for the New Story

By 2025 the earnings releases increasingly described Quanta around load growth, not just the energy transition. The July 2025 Dynamic Systems acquisition release spoke directly about technology, semiconductor, healthcare and other load-center markets, while the October 2025 NiSource announcement showed Quanta stretching beyond electric and mechanical facility scope into a broader generation-and-grid response to large-load demand. In that release, Quanta said NiSource had engaged it for generation and infrastructure resources capable of producing approximately 3 gigawatts of power for a large-load customer. [Dynamic Systems Acquisition](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/380/quanta-services-acquires-dynamic-systems-a-premier-turnkey-mechanical-and-process-infrastructure-solutions-provider) [NiSource Large-Load Announcement](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/386/building-upon-decades-of-power-generation-experience-quanta-expands-its-total-solutions-platform-and-announces-its-selection-by-nisource-to-provide-power-generation-and-grid-infrastructure-solutions-for-a-large-load-customer)

That October 2025 announcement was especially important because it grounded the load-center thesis in a named, dated primary-source item rather than in conference-call color alone. It also broadened the commercial question. Quanta was no longer only selling construction services after a utility or hyperscaler had already settled its power plan; it was trying to insert itself earlier in the chain, spanning generation, battery storage, transmission, substation and underground infrastructure. [NiSource Large-Load Announcement](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/386/building-upon-decades-of-power-generation-experience-quanta-expands-its-total-solutions-platform-and-announces-its-selection-by-nisource-to-provide-power-generation-and-grid-infrastructure-solutions-for-a-large-load-customer)

## The Numbers Caught Up With the Narrative

The results releases through early 2026 showed the financial statements catching up with that operating story. Full-year 2025 revenue was $28.48 billion, net income attributable to common stock $1.03 billion, adjusted diluted EPS $10.75, year-end RPO $23.76 billion and total backlog $43.98 billion. Then, on April 30, 2026, Quanta reported first-quarter revenue of $7.87 billion, adjusted diluted EPS of $2.68, RPO of $26.2 billion and total backlog of $48.5 billion, and raised substantially all of its 2026 financial expectations. [Q4 & FY2025 Results](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/390/quanta-services-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results) [Q1 2026 Results](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/396/quanta-services-reports-first-quarter-2026-results)

The resulting earnings story was more disciplined than the old draft's line about a single AI epiphany. Quanta had built a revenue base around grid and renewable work first, layered in Cupertino's electrical data-center capability in mid-2024, extended the load-center thesis with Dynamic Systems in mid-2025, and by late 2025 was publicly attaching its name to large-load generation and grid solutions with NiSource. In that sense the earnings story was not one headline event. It was a sequence of disclosed operating expansions that eventually made the headline backlog and guidance increases believable. [Cupertino Electric Acquisition](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/360/quanta-services-acquires-cupertino-electric-inc-a-premier-electrical-infrastructure-solutions-provider-to-the-technology-and-renewable-energy-industries) [Dynamic Systems Acquisition](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/380/quanta-services-acquires-dynamic-systems-a-premier-turnkey-mechanical-and-process-infrastructure-solutions-provider) [NiSource Large-Load Announcement](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/386/building-upon-decades-of-power-generation-experience-quanta-expands-its-total-solutions-platform-and-announces-its-selection-by-nisource-to-provide-power-generation-and-grid-infrastructure-solutions-for-a-large-load-customer)

chapters.title: Duke Austin, Jayshree Desai CFO, segment presidents, and the Foster-Lead-Independent board
chapters.body:
## Duke Austin's Tenure, Corrected

The prior draft's leadership chapter was materially wrong on both biography and current governance. Quanta's own releases said Earl C. "Duke" Austin joined Quanta in 2001, led North Houston Pole Line until 2009, joined the Quanta executive team in 2009, became chief operating officer in January 2013 and was named president and chief executive officer on March 14, 2016. Quanta's management page said he held a B.S. in Business Management/Accounting from Sam Houston State University. He therefore did not arrive through a 2003 PAR acquisition, and he did not hold the Texas A&M construction-management background attributed to him in the prior draft. [CEO Transition](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/202/quanta-services-announces-ceo-transition-chief-operating-officer-earl-duke-austin-named-chief-executive-officer) [Management Team](https://investors.quantaservices.com/company-information/management-team)

That mattered not only as a biographical clean-up but as a strategic point. Austin's tenure covered the period in which Quanta shifted from a grid-and-pipeline contractor into a larger utility, renewable, technology and load-center infrastructure platform. By the end of 2025, annual revenue had reached $28.48 billion and year-end backlog $43.98 billion; by the first quarter of 2026 backlog had risen again to $48.5 billion. Quanta's public materials in that period repeatedly described the strategy in operational terms, centering craft labor, execution certainty, supply-chain investments and collaborative solutions rather than financial engineering. [Q4 & FY2025 Results](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/390/quanta-services-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results) [Q1 2026 Results](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/396/quanta-services-reports-first-quarter-2026-results)

## Jayshree Desai and the Finance Function

The prior draft's description of Jayshree Desai was also stale. Quanta disclosed in May 2022 that Desai, then chief corporate development officer, would become chief financial officer effective in July 2022. Its management page said she had joined Quanta in January 2020 and before that had served as CFO of EDP Renewables North America, COO of Clean Line Energy Partners and president of ConnectGen. She therefore was not an external CFO hire arriving from ChampionX in late 2022; she was an internal executive who had already been running M&A and treasury functions before taking the top finance job. [Executive Transitions](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/319/quanta-services-announces-planned-executive-transitions) [Management Team](https://investors.quantaservices.com/company-information/management-team)

That distinction mattered because Quanta's 2024-2026 capital-allocation story was acquisition-heavy. The fourth-quarter 2025 release said Quanta completed eight acquisitions during 2025, and the proxy's named-executive-officer discussion centered on a leadership team that had to digest those deals while still lifting organic growth. Having a CFO who had already been leading corporate development was materially different from parachuting in an outside operator to digest acquisitions after the fact. [Quanta FY2025 Results](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/390/quanta-services-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results) [2026 Proxy Statement](https://investors.quantaservices.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001193125-26-150293/d118470ddef14a.htm)

## The Operating Bench as of the Frozen Date

The old bench description, centered on Redgie Probst, Scott Beck and Tim Heenan as three segment presidents, no longer reflected Quanta's actual disclosed leadership. Quanta's management page showed BJ Ducey as president of strategic operations, where he led the team evaluating technologies, assets, projects and opportunities across Quanta's growing portfolio. The same page showed Karl Studer as president of electric power, directly overseeing Quanta's electrical operations across the United States, Canada and Australia. Donald Wayne served as executive vice president and general counsel, bringing more than 25 years of legal experience, including more than 20 years as general counsel to energy and construction companies. [Management Team](https://investors.quantaservices.com/company-information/management-team)

The proxy's named-executive-officer disclosures likewise centered on Austin, Desai, Studer, Ducey and Wayne rather than the outdated segment-president roster in the prior draft. That updated bench also lined up with the reorganized company. Once Quanta merged electric and renewable reporting into a single Electric segment and began adding load-center electrical and mechanical scope, the older three-president framing had become less useful. The company was presenting a leadership team built around cross-platform strategy, electric operations, finance and legal execution rather than around the old three-way segment map. [2026 Proxy Statement](https://investors.quantaservices.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001193125-26-150293/d118470ddef14a.htm) [Q1 2025 Results](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/374/quanta-services-reports-first-quarter-2025-results)

## Governance: No More Lead-Independent-Director Framework

The prior draft's governance section was the most visibly stale. By the 2026 proxy, Quanta explicitly highlighted a leadership structure with a separate independent chairman and chief executive officer. Doyle N. Beneby, who had been on the board since 2016, was identified as chairman of the board. The proxy also showed a board architecture built around audit, compensation, governance and nominating, finance and investment, and safety, operations and risk committees. That meant the old lead-independent-director description centered on Vincent D. Foster was no longer current as of the frozen window. [2026 Proxy Statement](https://investors.quantaservices.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001193125-26-150293/d118470ddef14a.htm)

The board composition had also moved on. The 2026 proxy named Austin, Beneby, Warner Baxter, Bernard Fried, Worthing Jackman, Holli Ladhani, Jo-ann dePass Olsovsky, R. Scott Rowe, Martha Wyrsch and Joseph Kim as the slate, and described Quanta's nominees as bringing a mix of utility, operations, risk, governance and strategic-planning experience. Quanta then announced on May 22, 2026 that Joseph Kim had joined the board, emphasizing his executive leadership, operations, supply-chain and logistics experience. [2026 Proxy Statement](https://investors.quantaservices.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001193125-26-150293/d118470ddef14a.htm) [Joseph Kim Joins Board](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/398/joseph-kim-joins-quanta-services-board-of-directors)

## What the Corrected Leadership Story Suggested

The corrected leadership picture was less romantic than the older field-general narrative, but more analytically useful. Austin was still clearly an operator, yet he was an operator who rose through Quanta's own internal structure and then presided over a board that, by 2026, had been refreshed toward utility, industrial, technology, logistics and public-company operating oversight. Desai was not a late outside arrival but an internal capital-allocation lieutenant promoted into the CFO seat in mid-2022. The resulting leadership architecture looked designed for a company that expected more acquisitions, more load-growth programs and a bigger interface with utility and technology customers than the legacy segment structure implied. [Management Team](https://investors.quantaservices.com/company-information/management-team) [2026 Proxy Statement](https://investors.quantaservices.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001193125-26-150293/d118470ddef14a.htm)

chapters.title: IOUs, hyperscalers, renewable developers, and the workforce-and-equipment supply chain
chapters.body:
Quanta's customer map by the frozen date was both broader and more quantifiable than the prior draft suggested. In the 2025 10-K, Quanta said customer-type estimates were 70% Utility and Power, 17% Energy and Other, and 13% Technology, Manufacturing and Communications, versus 74%, 17% and 9% in 2024 and 75%, 19% and 6% in 2023. That meant the technology/manufacturing/communications slice had more than doubled in mix over two years, but utility and power still remained the clear base business. [2025 10-K](https://investors.quantaservices.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001050915-26-000006/pwr-20251231.htm)

| Customer type | 2023 | 2024 | 2025 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Utility and Power | 75% | 74% | 70% |
| Energy and Other | 19% | 17% | 17% |
| Technology, Manufacturing and Communications | 6% | 9% | 13% |

## The IOU and Power-Developer Core

The company still looked most like a utility contractor when viewed through its representative-customer list. The 2025 10-K named American Electric Power, CenterPoint, Duke Energy, Entergy, Exelon, FirstEnergy, Hydro One, Idaho Power, National Grid, NextEra, NiSource, PG&E, Puget Sound Energy, Sempra, Southern Company and Xcel among representative customers, alongside power developers such as Engie IR Holdings, Invenergy, Pattern Energy and the Iberdrola and RWE groups. That customer set was broader and more specific than the older draft's partly inferred list. [2025 10-K](https://investors.quantaservices.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001050915-26-000006/pwr-20251231.htm)

Customer concentration remained present but not extreme. For 2025, Quanta said its largest customer accounted for 8% of consolidated revenue and its ten largest customers for 30%. The same filing said Quanta had developed strong strategic alliances with numerous customers and sought preferred-solutions-provider status. That was an important corrective to any view that the company had become a one-customer or one-cycle proxy. Even after Cupertino and Dynamic Systems, Quanta was still disclosing a diversified base of repeat utility, developer, communications and industrial relationships. [2025 10-K](https://investors.quantaservices.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001050915-26-000006/pwr-20251231.htm)

## Cupertino's Technology Bridge

The prior draft was directionally right that Cupertino changed Quanta's customer exposure, but the official release gave a more precise description than the dossier had. Quanta said Cupertino had a 25-year working history with global technology-industry leaders and had installed electrical systems in more than 20 million square feet of data centers. The acquisition therefore gave Quanta a direct operating bridge into the technology and large-load customer set, not merely a speculative adjacency to it. [Cupertino Electric Acquisition](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/360/quanta-services-acquires-cupertino-electric-inc-a-premier-electrical-infrastructure-solutions-provider-to-the-technology-and-renewable-energy-industries)

Quanta reinforced that message in the third-quarter 2024 release, saying Cupertino integration was progressing well and that customers were responding positively to a combined critical-path electrical offering for technology and data-center projects. That was the clearest primary-source support for the idea that Quanta saw utilities and hyperscale-adjacent customers converging around the same need: more power, delivered faster, with fewer labor and supply-chain bottlenecks. [Q3 2024 Results](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/367/quanta-services-reports-third-quarter-2024-results)

## The Load-Center and Generation Expansion

By late 2025 Quanta had moved beyond pure electrical scope. The Dynamic Systems acquisition added a mechanical and process-infrastructure provider serving technology, semiconductor, healthcare and other load-center markets, with roughly 2,400 employees and an estimated 2026 revenue contribution of $1.25 billion to $1.45 billion. Three months later, Quanta announced that NiSource had engaged it for generation and grid infrastructure resources capable of producing approximately 3 gigawatts of power for a large-load customer. Those two disclosures together were more concrete evidence of Quanta's customer expansion than the old draft's unsupported references to unnamed hyperscalers and giant power commitments. [Dynamic Systems Acquisition](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/380/quanta-services-acquires-dynamic-systems-a-premier-turnkey-mechanical-and-process-infrastructure-solutions-provider) [NiSource Large-Load Announcement](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/386/building-upon-decades-of-power-generation-experience-quanta-expands-its-total-solutions-platform-and-announces-its-selection-by-nisource-to-provide-power-generation-and-grid-infrastructure-solutions-for-a-large-load-customer)

## Labor Pipeline, Fleet and Supply Chain

The workforce and equipment statistics also required correction. As of December 31, 2025, Quanta said it had approximately 69,500 employees, including about 13,800 salaried employees and about 55,700 hourly employees. It also said its owned and leased fleet totaled about 80,000 units. Those figures were materially larger and more precise than the ad hoc workforce estimates and unsupported self-perform statistics in the prior draft. [2025 10-K](https://investors.quantaservices.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001050915-26-000006/pwr-20251231.htm)

The labor-pipeline architecture behind those numbers was more developed than the prior draft showed. Quanta's 2018 release on Northwest Lineman College said the school had trained approximately 5,600 people in 2017. By the 2024 sustainability report, Quanta said campus programs at NLC trained 7,406 students, the Quanta Advanced Training Center trained 1,312 Quanta employees and Stronghold University trained 8,649. The same report described the Quanta Advanced Training Center at the 2,600-acre Lazy Q Ranch in La Grange, Texas, underscoring that Quanta had chosen to internalize a significant share of the labor pipeline rather than rely solely on spot-market hiring. [NLC Acquisition](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/238/quanta-services-acquires-northwest-lineman-college) [2024 Sustainability Report Metrics](https://sustainability.quantaservices.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/2024-Quanta-Sustainability-Report-Pages.pdf)

On supply chain, the strongest supportable item was not the previously cited Pennsylvania Transformer Technology anecdote but Quanta's own risk language and acquisition disclosures. The 2025 10-K warned that transformer availability had been negatively affected by manufacturers' inability to meet current market demand. Separately, the third-quarter 2024 release disclosed that Quanta had completed the acquisition of a Buffalo, New York-based manufacturer with a 100-year operating history that specialized in medium-voltage, liquid-filled power transformers. That gave the dossier a real primary-source basis for saying Quanta was trying to pull at least one constrained electrical input closer to its operating platform. [2025 10-K](https://investors.quantaservices.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001050915-26-000006/pwr-20251231.htm) [Q3 2024 Results](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/367/quanta-services-reports-third-quarter-2024-results)

## What the Customer Map Actually Showed

What emerged from the corrected sourcing was a company whose base was still utility and power, whose developer relationships remained important through renewables, and whose fastest-changing edge sat in the technology, manufacturing and communications bucket. That bucket was still only 13% of 2025 revenue by Quanta's own estimate, so the company had not become a pure AI-infrastructure proxy. But it had clearly become more exposed to large-load and digital-infrastructure customers than the 2023 mix would have implied, and it had been investing in training, fleet and selected supply-chain assets to support that shift. [2025 10-K](https://investors.quantaservices.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001050915-26-000006/pwr-20251231.htm)

chapters.title: Where Quanta sits against MasTec, MYR Group, Primoris, broader specialty contractor set
chapters.body:
## Scale Relative to Public Peers

By the frozen date, Quanta remained in a different revenue class from the North American specialty-contracting peers most often cited alongside it. Quanta generated $28.48 billion of revenue in 2025. MasTec generated $14.3 billion in 2025. Primoris generated $7.57 billion in 2025. MYR Group generated $3.66 billion in 2025. Dycom generated $5.55 billion of contract revenue in its fiscal year ended January 31, 2026. Fiscal calendars and segment definitions were not identical, but the size gap was still unmistakable. [Quanta FY2025 Results](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/390/quanta-services-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results) [MasTec FY2025 Results](https://investors.mastec.com/news-releases/news-release-details/mastec-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-financial) [Primoris FY2025 Results](https://ir.prim.com/news-and-events/news-releases/2026/02-23-2026-211611532) [MYR FY2025 Results](https://investor.myrgroup.com/news-releases/news-release-details/myr-group-inc-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025) [Dycom FY2026 Results](https://dycomind.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Q4-2026-Results-Release.pdf)

| Company | Ticker | Latest annual revenue before frozen date | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Quanta Services | PWR | $28.48B | 2025 calendar year |
| MasTec | MTZ | $14.3B | 2025 calendar year |
| Primoris | PRIM | $7.57B | 2025 calendar year |
| Dycom | DY | $5.55B | Fiscal year ended Jan. 31, 2026 |
| MYR Group | MYRG | $3.66B | 2025 calendar year |

Quanta therefore stood at roughly twice MasTec's scale, nearly four times Primoris, more than five times Dycom and almost eight times MYR by revenue. Arithmetic made the separation even clearer. Quanta's Electric segment alone produced $23.00 billion of 2025 revenue, which was greater than the combined latest annual revenue of Primoris, MYR and Dycom at roughly $16.78 billion, and also larger than MasTec's entire company. The point was not that bigger was automatically better. It was that Quanta's scale advantage was large enough to matter when utilities, developers and large-load customers were deciding which contractor could actually mobilize labor, equipment and project controls at program scale. [Quanta FY2025 Results](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/390/quanta-services-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results) [Primoris FY2025 Results](https://ir.prim.com/news-and-events/news-releases/2026/02-23-2026-211611532) [MYR FY2025 Results](https://investor.myrgroup.com/news-releases/news-release-details/myr-group-inc-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025) [Dycom FY2026 Results](https://dycomind.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Q4-2026-Results-Release.pdf) [MasTec FY2025 Results](https://investors.mastec.com/news-releases/news-release-details/mastec-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-financial)

## MasTec: The Only Close-Enough Scale Peer

MasTec remained the closest public comparator because it still had multi-segment exposure across power delivery, communications, pipeline and clean-energy infrastructure. But the 2025 results showed that it was still materially smaller than Quanta on both revenue and backlog framing. MasTec reported $14.3 billion of 2025 revenue and a record 18-month backlog of $19.0 billion. Quanta reported $28.48 billion of 2025 revenue and year-end backlog of $43.98 billion, though Quanta's backlog definition was not directly comparable because it included estimated orders under MSAs and short-term, non-fixed price contracts. [MasTec FY2025 Results](https://investors.mastec.com/news-releases/news-release-details/mastec-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-financial) [Quanta FY2025 Results](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/390/quanta-services-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results) [Q1 2026 10-Q](https://investors.quantaservices.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001050915-26-000016/pwr-20260331.htm)

The strategic difference by 2026 was breadth at the electrical-and-load-center intersection. Quanta had combined utility grid work, utility-scale renewables, inside-electric data-center capability through Cupertino and, after 2025, mechanical/process infrastructure through Dynamic Systems. Its own 2025 10-K said it believed it could offer critical-path low-voltage electrical systems inside data centers, the high-voltage interconnection infrastructure needed to connect those facilities to the grid, and generation infrastructure necessary to power them. MasTec still had a broader pipeline and communications mix, but Quanta's operating story around power demand, generation, grid expansion and load-center delivery had become more tightly integrated. [2025 10-K](https://investors.quantaservices.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001050915-26-000006/pwr-20251231.htm) [Cupertino Electric Acquisition](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/360/quanta-services-acquires-cupertino-electric-inc-a-premier-electrical-infrastructure-solutions-provider-to-the-technology-and-renewable-energy-industries) [Dynamic Systems Acquisition](https://investors.quantaservices.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/380/quanta-services-acquires-dynamic-systems-a-premier-turnkey-mechanical-and-process-infrastructure-solutions-provider)

## Primoris and MYR: Real Competitors, Narrower Frames

Primoris and MYR were both real operating competitors, but each occupied a narrower frame. Primoris reported $7.57 billion of 2025 revenue, including $2.69 billion in Utilities and $5.02 billion in Energy. That clearly made it relevant in power delivery, renewables and parts of industrial construction. But it was still much smaller than Quanta and did not disclose anything like Quanta's electrical-plus-mechanical load-center platform. [Primoris FY2025 Results](https://ir.prim.com/news-and-events/news-releases/2026/02-23-2026-211611532)

MYR, meanwhile, remained the closest pure-play electrical contractor in public-company form. It reported $2.00 billion of 2025 Transmission & Distribution revenue and $1.66 billion of Commercial & Industrial revenue, for $3.66 billion consolidated. That made MYR a serious competitor in selected T&D and commercial electrical programs, but not a portfolio-level analogue for Quanta's combination of grid, renewables, large-load electrical and newer generation-related scope. [MYR FY2025 Results](https://investor.myrgroup.com/news-releases/news-release-details/myr-group-inc-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025)

## Dycom: Useful Contrast, Different Core

Dycom belonged in the comparison set largely as a contrast. It reported record fiscal 2026 contract revenue of $5.55 billion, but its underlying franchise remained telecom and digital-connectivity infrastructure rather than electric grid, renewables or power generation. Dycom therefore highlighted how unusual Quanta's positioning had become: Quanta was trying to sit where rising power demand, renewable interconnection, data-center electrical systems and selected mechanical critical-path work all met. [Dycom FY2026 Results](https://dycomind.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Q4-2026-Results-Release.pdf)

## The Real Competitive Question

The corrected competitive question was therefore not whether Quanta had peers; it plainly did. The question was whether any peer combined enough of the same constrained capabilities in one public vehicle to pressure Quanta on price and labor at the exact same time across utility, renewable and large-load programs. By the frozen date, MasTec was the closest broad-platform rival. MYR was the closest electrical pure-play. Primoris was the credible mid-scale renewable-and-utility alternative. Dycom was the digital-infrastructure outlier. None of them, based on their own disclosures, matched Quanta's revenue scale plus the acquired mix of Blattner, Cupertino and Dynamic Systems, or the specific integrated stack Quanta described in its own 10-K. [MasTec FY2025 Results](https://investors.mastec.com/news-releases/news-release-details/mastec-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-financial) [Primoris FY2025 Results](https://ir.prim.com/news-and-events/news-releases/2026/02-23-2026-211611532) [MYR FY2025 Results](https://investor.myrgroup.com/news-releases/news-release-details/myr-group-inc-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025) [Dycom FY2026 Results](https://dycomind.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Q4-2026-Results-Release.pdf) [2025 10-K](https://investors.quantaservices.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001050915-26-000006/pwr-20251231.htm)
